nodeData.note: SB 1.15.16 · a class by HG Sri Gauranga Das. Arjuna, in the mood of separation, remembers how the greatest generals of the Kuru army could not harm him because Krishna protected him as He protected Prahlad. Prabhu tells the stories behind Bhishma, Drona, Karna, Bhurishrava and Jayadrat, answers the charge that Krishna cheated on the battlefield, and explains that the Lord had already decided the outcome and arranged everything to give credit to His devotees. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Arjuna tells Yudhishthira that the weapons of the mightiest Kuru generals could not even touch his hair, because Krishna protected him.

Under normal circumstances the war could not be won. Prabhu explains that an akshauhini is a full phalanx of soldiers, cavalry, elephants and chariots; the Pandavas had seven and the Kauravas eleven, along with the finest warriors.

🎙 Prabhu at 16:37 (auto-transcript): “in ordinary circumstances, it was impossible to win the war against the Kauravas. The Kauravas had a greater army in terms of numbers, the Pandavas managed to get seven Akshahinis. As Srila Prabhupada is mentioning here, Akshahini is like a phalanx that comprises of an army,…”

At the start of the Gita Duryodhana lists his great fighters to his teacher Drona and feels his side, guarded by Bhishma, is far stronger. Bhishma had an unbroken record, yet the Pandavas won because Krishna protected them.

🎙 Prabhu at 17:46 (auto-transcript): “warriors. In the beginning of the Bhagat Gita, Duryodhana goes to his teacher Dronacharya and he is telling his teacher Dronacharya, he says, I have great soldiers on my side. He is telling Dronacharya that I have you I have Bhishma I have Karna I have Somadhat I have Kripa I…”

Arjuna is not comparing himself to Prahlad. He is marvelling that the Pandavas received the same protection the Lord gave His dear devotee Prahlad. — “He is saying, we got the same mercy that Prahlad got.”

🎙 Prabhu at 20:05 (auto-transcript): “Just like he protected Prahlad Maharaj. Arjuna, he is considering his great fortune, how Lord Krishna protected him and his brothers in the same vein that Lord Krishna protected his great devotee, Prahlad Maharaj. Arjuna here is not comparing himself to Prahlad Maharaj, no.…”

Arjuna has just told Yudhishthira that Krishna has left the earth. In this world people usually value their own life above everyone when things get dire, but for the Pandavas Krishna was dearer than life. — “for the Pandavas Lord Krishna was dearer to them than their own lives”

🎙 Prabhu at 14:16 (auto-transcript): “Arjuna is remembering his interactions with the Supreme Lord as he is speaking to Yudhishthir Maharaj after informing Yudhishthir Maharaj that his dear most object of affection Lord Sri Krishna is no longer here on this earth for the Pandavas Lord Krishna was dearer to them…”

children.topic: Viraha bhava: the mood of separation
children.note:
Arjuna's usual mood is friendship, sakhya rasa, but now it is overtaken by separation. He relives his days with the Lord in deep remembrance.

🎙 Prabhu at 15:43 (auto-transcript): “bhava is known as Viraha bhava, the mood of separation from the most beloved object. Ordinarily Arjuna is situated in the mood of friendship, sakhyaras. But that mood is sometimes overtaken by different situations. And so now we find that in this particular situation where…”

Lying on the bed of arrows, Bhishma meditated on Krishna's battlefield form — curly hair, sweat, dust from the horses, and wounds from Bhishma's own arrows. Bhishma could not touch Arjuna, yet Krishna let Bhishma pierce Him.

🎙 Prabhu at 21:25 (auto-transcript): “and we know from the earlier chapter Pishmadev he is lying on the bed of arrows defeated by Arjuna and he is praying to Lord Krishna meditating on that beautiful form of Lord Krishna that was present on the battlefield with long curly black hair and the forehead with beads of…”

Both sides held devotees: Bhishma, a mahajana, and Arjuna, the Lord's intimate friend. Krishna protected one and accepted the other's arrows — an exchange only those in relationship with Him can understand. — “So this is the wonderful exchange of the Lord with his devotees.”

🎙 Prabhu at 22:54 (auto-transcript): “on both sides were devotees Bhishma Dev was a great devotee He is Mahajan And on this side Arjuna is the most intimate devotee of the Lord And Lord Krishna is in between the two And Arjuna is saying Lord Krishna protected me But when it came to Bhishma Lord Krishna…”

Bhishma vowed to Duryodhana that either he or Arjuna would leave the field next day. When Arjuna was overwhelmed, Krishna jumped down, grabbed a broken wheel and charged Bhishma, breaking His own promise to save Arjuna and to honour Bhishma's vow.

🎙 Prabhu at 23:48 (auto-transcript): “And when the two devotees came to a head-to-head, Bishmadev, we all know, previous night he promised to Duryodhana that tomorrow morning either I will be taken off the battlefield or Arjuna will be taken off the battlefield. And the next morning, Bishmadev, he fought with so…”

children.topic: Drona: the guru on the other side
children.note:
Arjuna at first refused to kill his worshippable teacher, who taught him archery. Duryodhana was proud that Bhishma and Drona, despite their affection for the Pandavas, stayed with him out of obligation.

🎙 Prabhu at 25:19 (auto-transcript): “he protected me from my Guru Drona in the beginning of the battle Arjuna was refusing to fight saying Guru Nahatvahi Mahanubhava how can I kill my own Guru he is telling Lord Krishna you never killed your Guru how can you tell me to kill my Guru Guru is worshippable And Guru…”

Karna was Kunti's son by the sun god, but not a Pandava, since Pandava means son of Pandu.

🎙 Prabhu at 26:37 (auto-transcript): “So we see Śrīla Prabhupāda, he is giving a background of Karna. Karna was also son of Kunti, but he was not a Pandava. Pandava means sons of Pandu. And Karna, he was son of Kunti, given to her by the sun god, Suryadeva. We were reading about Durvasa a few verses back. Arjuna…”

Durvasa gave Kunti a mantra to call any demigod. Testing it, she called the sun god, who would not leave without giving the son the mantra asked for, promising her virginity would stay intact. Unmarried, she set the baby afloat on the Ganga in a basket.

🎙 Prabhu at 27:14 (auto-transcript): “The same Durvasa Muni had given Kunti Maharani one mantra that she can call any demigod she wants with this mantra. And so after Durvasa left, Kunti Maharani thought, let me test if this mantra actually works. And she saw the sun and she decided, let me call the sun god. And…”

Raised by Adiratha and his wife Radha, Karna was called Radheya — a name people wrongly link to Srimati Radharani. Prabhu calls him the tragic hero of the Mahabharata: from birth to death there was no happiness. — “Everything was a tragedy for him.”

🎙 Prabhu at 28:46 (auto-transcript): “and later on of course he was picked up by Adirat and his wife Radha and so Karna's other name was Radheya people think Radheya is related to Srimati Radharani, but no, Radheya is related to Karna. He was son of Radha, so Radheya. And from before, from his birth, Karna is…”

Again and again Karna was shut out, and he came to feel that great injustice was being done to him.

🎙 Prabhu at 29:32 (auto-transcript): “Dronacharya would teach him but would give Arjuna some more instructions over Karna. When it came time for graduation, Dronacharya barred Karna from graduating. He said, no, no, this graduation is only for those who are twice born. So everyone knew Karna was not a member of…”

Drona gave Arjuna extra instruction and, to keep Arjuna the best student, barred Karna from the graduation as not twice-born.

🎙 Prabhu at 29:41 (auto-transcript): “When it came time for graduation, Dronacharya barred Karna from graduating. He said, no, no, this graduation is only for those who are twice born. So everyone knew Karna was not a member of the twice born families. And so, therefore, because Dronacharya knew if Karna…”

Draupadi knew Karna was an excellent archer and declared beforehand that she would marry only a twice-born, so he was taken off the list.

🎙 Prabhu at 30:21 (auto-transcript): “and then again we read Srila Prabhupada speaking about how Karna came for Draupadi's Swayamvar and Draupadi also knew Karna is a very very good warrior excellent archer and so from before only she barred Karna from taking part in the competition, she said I will not marry…”

Duryodhana saw Karna's hurt, made him king of Anga at the graduation and befriended him, then kept fuelling his hatred of the Pandavas till Karna's death. — “he was only corrupted because Duryodhana took advantage of that.”

🎙 Prabhu at 31:04 (auto-transcript): “And although he had this grudge for injustice, he was only corrupted because Duryodhana took advantage of that. He saw that, oh, Karna is feeling that he is being treated badly. So let me make friendship with him. And it was during that ceremony, the graduation ceremony, when…”

Kunti came with Krishna and told Karna he was her son, asking him not to kill her sons. Upset that she came only now, he promised she would always have five sons: either he or Arjuna would live.

🎙 Prabhu at 32:25 (auto-transcript): “Just before the war, actually Kunti Maharani came to Karna with Lord Krishna. And she explained to Karna, she said, see, you're actually my son. And Karna was very upset with the mother, with Kunti. And said, so why have you come all these years? After all these years, why…”

Many use Karna as an example of injustice and say Krishna won the war for the Pandavas by unfair means.

🎙 Prabhu at 33:35 (auto-transcript): “Many people, they use him as an example of injustice that was done in the war. They don't understand. Here Arjuna is saying, it's actually Krishna who protected me from all these great warriors. But people point Krishna and they say, no, Krishna made the Pandavas win through…”

children.note:
Karna's charioteer was already dead, so he got down to free the stuck wheel himself. Arjuna stopped, since the kshatriya code forbids fighting an opponent who is unarmed or not ready.

🎙 Prabhu at 33:59 (auto-transcript): “When Karna's wheel got stuck and he got down from his chariot to lift his wheel, one can wonder what was the charioteer doing but the charioteer had already gone. He was dead. So he couldn't actually. Karna was left on his chariot without a charioteer and the wheel got stuck.…”

children.topic: Where was the code for Abhimanyu?
children.note:
Krishna told Arjuna to shoot, reminding him that seven generals, Karna among them, had together killed sixteen-year-old Abhimanyu. Karna begged for a warrior's death, but Arjuna fired.

🎙 Prabhu at 35:16 (auto-transcript): “and Lord Krishna looked at Arjuna and told him what are you doing? Why are you waiting? Kill him! Lord Krishna how do I kill? He is a Kshatriya I am a Kshatriya we have to follow the code of conduct between Kshatriyas He said where was his Kshatriya when he killed your son…”

So-called moralists also cite Shikhandi placed before Bhishma, and the elephant named Ashwatthama killed so Drona would hear his son had died.

🎙 Prabhu at 36:32 (auto-transcript): “so many people look at this incident and they say see Lord Krishna cheated even with Bhishma Lord Krishna cheated he put Shikhandi in front of Arjuna and Bhishma didn't fight and so therefore he was defeated even with Drona Lord Krishna cheated he told Bhima to kill…”

In the universal form, as time, Krishna showed Arjuna the warriors already caught in His teeth — Duryodhana's party like moths into fire, sympathisers like Bhishma and Drona like rivers into the ocean. They came with a one-way ticket; only the Pandavas would return, and Krishna arranged it all to give His devotees the credit. — “Arjuna was simply an instrument.”

🎙 Prabhu at 37:38 (auto-transcript): “we know from the Gita, Lord Krishna had already killed everyone. Arjuna saw this. When Lord Krishna revealed his Vishwarupa, his universal form, Arjuna saw all these soldiers rushing into the mouth of Lord Krishna. He saw the terrible teeth of Lord Krishna. In his form as…”

Prabhu adds background to Srila Prabhupada's notes on the other generals Arjuna names.

🎙 Prabhu at 39:59 (auto-transcript): “Now here Srila Prabhupada is mentioning that Burishrava was very much enthused to see the valor of Arjuna, right? He is saying he appreciated the wonderful strength of Arjuna due to his being a devotee and friend of the Lord. So, Burishrava actually was sympathetic to the…”

Bhurishrava admired Arjuna and set out with a full akshauhini to fight for the Pandavas. Duryodhana's spies learned of it, and he built a city overnight on the way where the army was feasted like demigods; Bhurishrava vowed to fight for his hosts, and as a kshatriya had to keep his word when Duryodhana stepped out.

🎙 Prabhu at 40:19 (auto-transcript): “So, Burishrava actually was sympathetic to the Pandavas. And so, when they heard that the Pandavas and Kauravas were fighting, kings all over the world wanted to come and join. And so, Burishrava also decided he had one Akshahini, one whole complete Akshahini. He said, I will…”

children.topic: Jayadrat's head in his father's lap
children.note:
Lord Shiva had promised Jayadrat that whoever dropped his head to the ground would die. Krishna told Arjuna to send the head into his father's lap, keeping Shiva's word and protecting Arjuna.

🎙 Prabhu at 42:47 (auto-transcript): “We hear about Trigartha Susharma and his brother Jayadrat. And how Lord Krishna protected Jai Adrath from breaking Lord Shiva's promise. Lord Shiva had promised Jai Adrath that whoever throws your head on the ground will die. So to keep Shiva's promise and as well as to…”

Ordinarily the Pandavas could never have walked out of the battlefield alive. The intrigue people see only increases the sweetness of how the Lord protected them; tomorrow Arjuna's mood will go even deeper. — “All that is just to increase the sweetness of the Lord protecting the Pandavas.”

🎙 Prabhu at 43:25 (auto-transcript): “So, in this way, at every single step, every single moment, ordinarily, it wouldn't have been possible for the Pandavas to walk out unscathed and alive out of the battlefield. Parikshit Maharaj also knew this. When he is speaking to Shukadeva Goswami, he is telling Shukadeva…”

Parikshit asks Shukadeva for Krishna's pastimes because only by Him did his grandfathers cross an ocean full of great sharks. Meet a great white shark, Prabhu says, and you too go with a one-way ticket.

🎙 Prabhu at 43:46 (auto-transcript): “Parikshit Maharaj also knew this. When he is speaking to Shukadeva Goswami, he is telling Shukadeva Goswami, please tell me about the activities and pastimes of Lord Krishna. For it is only because of Lord Krishna that my grandfathers could overcome these great sharks in the…”

children.topic: Whom Krishna protects, none can kill
children.note:
Quoting the Caitanya-caritamrita, Prabhu says no one can kill whom the Lord protects, and no one can save whom He wants to kill — so great Bhishma, Drona and Karna had no protector.

🎙 Prabhu at 44:41 (auto-transcript): “And in the Chaitanya Charitamarta we hear Rake Krishna Mareke Mare Krishna Rakeke for a person who is protected by the Lord who can kill him and for a person who the Lord wants to kill who can protect him and so even though there were such great warriors Bhishma, Drona, Karna…”

Questions and comments at the end of the class.

🎙 Prabhu at 46:10 (auto-transcript): “if there are any questions or comments yes Sri Panukha Prabhu So how do we make common men understand that Krishna never cheated because Krishna is the source of morality Lord Krishna is the one who gives the codes of religion and ethics and morality”

How do we make ordinary people understand that Krishna, the source of morality, never cheated — when He also says that among cheaters He is the greatest?

🎙 Prabhu at 46:23 (auto-transcript): “So how do we make common men understand that Krishna never cheated because Krishna is the source of morality Lord Krishna is the one who gives the codes of religion and ethics and morality So how do we explain that Lord Krishna never cheated Lord Krishna also says in the Gita…”

Krishna had already decided the outcome; the rest was decoration to credit His devotees. One act of His fulfils many background stories, as Lord Nrisimha kept Brahma's boon intact yet killed Hiranyakashipu. To see this, a person must first understand who Krishna is.

🎙 Prabhu at 47:09 (auto-transcript): “Lord Krishna is the source of morality He never cheated As I explained He already had killed everyone These were just decorations That came later on Lord Krishna had already decided Everyone who is coming here is gone And so to give credit to his devotees to give credit to…”

A devotee asks about Yudhishthira being asked to tell Drona that his son had died.

🎙 Prabhu at 49:24 (auto-transcript): “No, but here the question is that Maharaj Yudhishthir was asked to Inform Dronacharya That his son has died”

The instruction came from the Lord, not an ordinary person, and what He says is the truth. Morality without devotion is useless, yet this is no licence for us to lie: we follow guru, scripture and the Lord, not our own intelligence. — “then that morality is useless.”

🎙 Prabhu at 50:14 (auto-transcript): “it is not just some ordinary person asking Maharaj Yudhishthir to lie it is the Lord and for the Lord what he says is the truth everything else is a lie that is why we are glorifying the devotees they do not question the motive of the Lord they simply surrender and they do…”

What should a disciple do when doubting the spiritual master's instruction?

🎙 Prabhu at 51:45 (auto-transcript): “following the instruction of the spiritual master when you are doubting the instruction.”

Arjuna raised his doubts with Krishna at every step but then did exactly what he was told, with no second question when told to kill Karna. If the guru is not physically present, he is present in his instructions, and we can consult senior godbrothers, godsisters and shiksha gurus. — “Simple, we ask the Guru.”

🎙 Prabhu at 52:33 (auto-transcript): “Simple, we ask the Guru. That is what Arjuna was doing. He was asking Krishna at every step. When he was doubtful about fighting the war, he surrendered on to the Lord and he said, Lord Krishna told Arjuna, you do as you see fit. but Arjuna said no I will do exactly as you…”

Is it right to say obligation comes before affection?

🎙 Prabhu at 54:19 (auto-transcript): “so is it right is it correct to say that obligation comes before affection not with Lord Krishna right we see when it came to Lord Krishna his greatest devotees they threw away their obligations and just followed their affection for Krishna obligations come”

children.note:

maps.title: SB classes 2026 · Class 11 · Bhaktivinoda Thakur, Seventh Goswami

nodeData.note: · a class by HG Sri Gauranga Das. On the appearance day of Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur, Prabhu explains why he is called the seventh Goswami: he restored Mahaprabhu's movement in its pure form after a dark age of deviant groups. He tells his life as Kedarnath Dutta — a gifted, questioning child, a magistrate who found the Bhagavatam, took shelter of Vaishnavas, wrote through the night, discovered Mahaprabhu's birthplace and jailed a false incarnation — and closes with his predictions, his eternal identity and his call to chant. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: A great acharya in our line
children.note:
Prabhu introduces the day as the appearance of Srila Sacchidananda Bhaktivinoda Thakur, a great acharya in our disciplic succession.

🎙 Prabhu at 01:44 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna. So today is the most auspicious day of the appearance of Sri Satchidananda Bhaktivinavad Thakur. Sri Satchidananda Bhaktivinavad Thakur is a great acharya in our disciplic succession. Our disciplic succession originates from Lord Krishna himself who gave the…”

The line begins with Krishna teaching Brahma, then Narada, Vyasa, Madhvacharya, Ishvara Puri, Caitanya Mahaprabhu, the six Goswamis, Baladeva Vidyabhushana and Vishvanatha Cakravarti, and then Bhaktivinoda Thakur. It is called Gaudiya because Mahaprabhu established the chanting of the holy names in Gauda.

🎙 Prabhu at 02:07 (auto-transcript): “disciplic succession. Our disciplic succession originates from Lord Krishna himself who gave the science of devotional service and transcendental knowledge to Lord Brahma. From Lord Brahma, he taught it to his son Narada who taught it to the great sage Vyasa and then it…”

children.topic: Dark ages and the seventh Goswami
children.note:
After Shyamananda, Narottama and Srinivasa preached widely in Bengal and Odisha, Mahaprabhu's teachings were lost or misrepresented and the movement's authenticity was questioned.

🎙 Prabhu at 04:13 (auto-transcript): “So, it entered into a very dark age. After the three Acharyas, Shamananda, Pandit, then we have Naratam Das Thakur, who were direct disciples of Jeeva Goswami and Srinivas Acharya, these three. They preached Mahaprabhu's movement extensively in Bengal, Odisha and neighboring…”

Every other sampradaya had an authorised commentary but the Gaudiyas did not, until Baladeva Vidyabhushana wrote the Govinda Bhashya, bringing a renaissance and recognition.

🎙 Prabhu at 05:13 (auto-transcript): “And so another great Acharya came, Baladev Vidyabhushan, who gave an authorized commentary known as Govinda Bhashya on the Gita. All the other sampradays, they had a commentary. Gaudiya Vaishnavas, they didn't have. And so Baladeva Vidya Bhushan provided that commentary. And…”

Then came another dark age of offshoots whose low character gave the movement a bad name. Some men dressed as women claiming to be Mahaprabhu's gopis, though He never had any, and calling oneself a Gaudiya Vaishnava drew contempt.

🎙 Prabhu at 05:58 (auto-transcript): “Many offshoots came about, deviances came about and the people who are representing this great line of disciplic succession were not doing justice at all to Mahaprabhu's movement. They were giving Mahaprabhu's movement a very bad name. So the other followers of tradition and…”

Bhaktivinoda Thakur re-established Mahaprabhu's teaching in its pure form and made sure it continues. Srila Prabhupada calls him the original preacher of pure Krishna consciousness in modern times. — “because he established again Mahaprabhu's movement in its pure form.”

🎙 Prabhu at 08:06 (auto-transcript): “So, Seventh Goswami, Bhaktivinan Thakur is given the title Seventh Goswami because he established again Mahaprabhu's movement in its pure form. He taught what Mahaprabhu had come to teach here and he made sure that it continues. So his contribution to our movement is…”

He was born Kedarnath Dutta into a wealthy, long-established family in Ula, Bengal, to Ananda Chandra and Jagan Mohini.

🎙 Prabhu at 08:53 (auto-transcript): “And so Bhaktivinoda Thakur was having a very illustrious life. He was earlier known as Kedarnath Dutta. His Western birth date was 2 September 1838, but devotees honour the Vedic date, the bright thirteenth day of the month of Bhadra.

🎙 Prabhu at 09:14 (auto-transcript): “So one may question then why are we speaking about him today? Why not on 2nd of September? But 2nd of September was his western calendar birth date. but according to the Vedic calendar he was born today which is the Shukla Trayodashi of the month of Badra. So in a few days we…”

children.topic: A poem at two, epics by six
children.note:
At two he composed a couplet telling a crow to move aside because his father was coming, and his father soon returned. Instead of playing he sat with the gatekeepers hearing the Ramayana and Mahabharata, and by ten he was asking who he is and why we are here.

🎙 Prabhu at 10:29 (auto-transcript): “he had composed a poem Bhaktivinoda Thakur was no ordinary child at the age of two when some children barely speak Bhaktivinoda Thakur had composed a poem regarding a crow he told the crow move aside my father is coming just two lines he had spoken at the age of two and a few…”

When he was eleven his father died; the family could not hold on to its wealth and fell into hardship.

🎙 Prabhu at 11:48 (auto-transcript): “But later on, a year later, when he was 11, his father passed away and Bhaktivinan Thakur and his family, or rather at that time he was known as Kedarnath Dutta, they went through financial hardship. All that generational wealth disappeared because Kedarnath was very young…”

He moved to Kolkata under his uncle, a well-known scholar and publisher. At a prestigious English school he met Western literature, wrote poetry and began questioning religion and philosophy.

🎙 Prabhu at 12:25 (auto-transcript): “So eventually he moved to Kolkata. He was born and brought up in Ulla, which is a place in West Bengal. But after his father passed away and they couldn't hold on to the wealth, he moved to Kolkata under his uncle and his uncle was a very well known scholar. His name was…”

He was already married at eleven to a five-year-old. Prabhu explains the old reasoning: each knew they had a spouse and would not look elsewhere, and the girl stayed home being trained until adolescence. In his autobiography he compared it to children playing with dolls. — “that this marriage was like dolls.”

🎙 Prabhu at 13:12 (auto-transcript): “Kolkata he was already married. Those days, they would get married at a very young age. He was 11, his wife was 5 years old. Her name was Shamani. So I am seeing some people laughing in the audience, but yeah, that was how it used to be. And there was a reason why. The reason…”

children.topic: When does wood become a deity?
children.note:
During Durga Puja he kept asking a carpenter when the carved wood becomes the deity — when the eyes were painted, when the brahmanas chanted — and each time said he saw nothing, until he was told it happens through mantra. He explored many faiths at a time when other sects flourished and Gaudiya Vaishnavism was looked down on.

🎙 Prabhu at 16:38 (auto-transcript): “One time during Durga Puja, Durga Puja is a very big festival in Bengal. It will happen in a few weeks time. Durga Puja. The whole of Bengal is celebrating this festival. And they fashion deities of Durga Ma from clay, from wood. So one time during that period, Kedarnath Dhat…”

Finding his village Ula devastated, he moved his family to Kolkata and began his working life while his philosophical search went on.

🎙 Prabhu at 19:09 (auto-transcript): “and then he started teaching in schools. He worked as a teacher and he was then promoted to a headmaster. He was teaching in Kendrapara school and then he was promoted to a headmaster in a school in Bhadrak and from there he went to a headmaster in Medhinipur. Medhinipur is…”

He rose from teacher to headmaster, then entered British government service and became a district magistrate — a post very rarely given to an Indian.

🎙 Prabhu at 19:15 (auto-transcript): “He worked as a teacher and he was then promoted to a headmaster. He was teaching in Kendrapara school and then he was promoted to a headmaster in a school in Bhadrak and from there he went to a headmaster in Medhinipur. Medhinipur is also quite famous in Bengal and then from…”

In Dinajpur he came across the Srimad-Bhagavatam and Caitanya-caritamrita, studied them intensely, and was convinced all his childhood questions were answered and no higher philosophy exists. He began lecturing on the Bhagavatam.

🎙 Prabhu at 20:54 (auto-transcript): “In Dinajpur something very significant happened. He came across copies of Srimad Bhagatam and Chaitanya Charita Amrita. When he got these copies of Srimad Bhagatam and Chaitanya Charita Amrita, he began studying them intensely. and he was convinced that all the questions he…”

Posted in Jagannath Puri, he met authentic Gaudiya Vaishnavas. Srila Jagannatha Dasa Babaji became his shiksha guru, and he took initiation from Vipin Vihari Goswami of Jahnava Mata's line, receiving the name Bhaktivinoda.

🎙 Prabhu at 21:43 (auto-transcript): “and in Jagannath Puri then he came into contact with Vaishnavas Godia Vaishnavas authentic Godia Vaishnavas he had already been familiarized with the Bhagatam and Chetanichari Tamrita and so when he went to Jagannath Puri he came into contact with Jagannath Das Babaji Maharaj…”

children.topic: Two hours' rest, writing all night
children.note:
Prabhu walks through his day: rest 8–10 pm, write until 4 am, a short rest, japa from 4:30 to 7, letters, shastra study, court 10–5 with lunch at home, translating Sanskrit into Bengali in the evening. His post was so high that a private rail line took him to the courthouse door.

🎙 Prabhu at 23:06 (auto-transcript): “he during this time he was doing his court duties but he was also writing a lot and what was his schedule like he would come back from work right and at 8 p.m he would take rest 8 to 10 p.m just two hours he would rest he would get up at 10 p.m and write all the way till 4…”

He wrote over a hundred books — among them Sri Krishna Samhita, Caitanya Shikshamrita, Harinama Cintamani, Jaiva Dharma and Bhajana Rahasya — and four books of songs such as Gitavali and Sharanagati, and he started publishing Vaishnava literature, all while in government service.

🎙 Prabhu at 25:12 (auto-transcript): “and in this way having association, writing books he wrote so many books some of his famous works are Shri Krishna Samhita, Chaitanya Chikshamrita Kalyana Kalpataru, Harinam Chintamani Jaiva Dharma, Bhajan Rahasya Sharanagati, Gita Mala, Gita Vali in these Gita Mala, Gita…”

Posted in Navadvip, he saw from his veranda a bright light on the empty far bank. Locals called it Mahaprabhu's real birthplace, and his research in old manuscripts and maps confirmed it.

🎙 Prabhu at 26:14 (auto-transcript): “so when he was posted in Navadvip that time Navadvip Navadvip means nine islands so Navadvip was exclusively on one side of the Ganga and the other side of the Ganges or the Ganga there was nothing and so one particular evening Bhaktivinoda Thakur was seated in his veranda…”

Jagannatha Dasa Babaji, too old to walk, was carried to the spot in a basket on his servant's back. There he leapt out and danced, and Bhaktivinoda Thakur went on to build the Yogapitha that pilgrims visit in Mayapur today. — “He said, yes, this is the birthplace of my Gora.”

🎙 Prabhu at 27:49 (auto-transcript): “So to confirm this, he called Jagannath Das Babaji Maharaj. That time, Jagannath Das Babaji Maharaj was so old, he was carried in a basket. He couldn't walk. His servant would carry him in a basket. Like how you carry a backpack, he would carry Jagannath Das Babaji Maharaj.…”

As magistrate he faced a yogi with real powers and a big following who claimed to be Mahavishnu and promised to destroy the British.

🎙 Prabhu at 28:51 (auto-transcript): “During his court duties, he got a report of a person named Bishakasen. Bishakasen was purporting to be Mahavishnu. He was telling his followers, the day will come soon that I will display my four-armed form and I will kill all these mlechas, the British government were and…”

children.topic: Abuse under the name of rasa
children.note:
The yogi demanded families send their girls to him for 'rasa-lila' at night. Families complained, and Bhaktivinoda Thakur investigated, gathered witnesses and brought him to court, unafraid of his threats.

🎙 Prabhu at 29:42 (auto-transcript): “So Bishak Hasein would tell the families, you send your young girls to me and at night we will perform Ras Leela and the families would be like why will we send our girls to you like no if you send your girl to me she will become blessed by me and some were forced some were…”

During eighteen days of hearings the yogi cursed the family; his daughter fell gravely ill and he himself had fever. His wife begged him to let the man go, but he insisted the rascal be punished. — “Bhaktivinod Thakur said, no, let us all die.”

🎙 Prabhu at 31:26 (auto-transcript): “And so Bishik Hasein was put into prison but while the court proceedings were going on, it was a long court proceeding, 18 days, 18 days of hearings. During those 18 days when this person was in prison, he cursed Kedarnath Dhat or Bhaktivinath Thakur's family. And…”

Learning the yogi's power lay in his hair, like Samson's, he went to the prison with guards and scissors and cut it off. The yogi fasted and died, and Navadvip was protected from bogus incarnations — the hardest of many such cases.

🎙 Prabhu at 32:34 (auto-transcript): “And then during those 18 days in the court, But as the proceedings were going on, Bhaktivinoda Thakur found out that this yogi, his power was in the hair. Something like Samson and Delilah, you know, that story. So in the Bible also, Samson had his power coming from hair. So…”

Bhaktivinoda Thakur kept writing and preaching with an international vision, wanting the whole world to come to Mayapur.

🎙 Prabhu at 34:15 (auto-transcript): “And in this way, Bhaktivinoda Thakur then continued writing, continued preaching in 1896, the year that Avayacharan Day was born, otherwise known as A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Srila Prabhupada. He had sent to the Western universities, universities in Germany, in Spain, in…”

He sent his writings to Western universities with an English booklet, The Life and Precepts of Caitanya Mahaprabhu, in the same year Srila Prabhupada was born. — “So this is not coincidence.”

🎙 Prabhu at 34:20 (auto-transcript): “continued preaching in 1896, the year that Avayacharan Day was born, otherwise known as A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Srila Prabhupada. He had sent to the Western universities, universities in Germany, in Spain, in France, he had sent them his writings accompanied by a 47-page…”

He foretold a personality who would spread Mahaprabhu's message everywhere, harinama in every country, and people of all backgrounds coming to Mayapur to chant with the Bengali Vaishnavas. Srila Prabhupada fulfilled all three.

🎙 Prabhu at 35:26 (auto-transcript): “And he made three predictions. He said soon there will be a personality who comes and who will take this message of Mahaprabhu all over the world. He will spread this message of Mahaprabhu all over the world. Second, he said, Harinam will be done all over the world. People…”

In Goloka he is Kamala Manjari, foremost assistant of Rupa Manjari under Lalita Sakhi, and his Navadvip house bears the name of her grove, Svananda Sukhada Kunja. So he is the foremost follower of Rupa Goswami. — “The foremost follower of Rupa Goswami is Bhaktivinan Thakur.”

🎙 Prabhu at 36:20 (auto-transcript): “And Bhaktivedanta Thakur in his own biography he writes about his eternal service to Shishi Radha and Krishna. He was known as Kamala Manjari and her residence, Kamala Manjari's residence is Svananda Sukhada Kunja. In Goloka Vrindavan, they have kunjas. Kunjas are like…”

He retired, took babaji initiation and spent his time chanting in Godrumadvipa, leaving the world in 1914.

🎙 Prabhu at 38:35 (auto-transcript): “In his final years, he withdrew from government service, he retired and exclusively he dedicated his time in chanting the holy names of the Lord. He took Babaji initiation, he became a Babaji and he was spending his entire time in Gudrumadvip, in Svananda Sukhadda Kunj,…”

In the song sung earlier he urges householder and sannyasi, happy or miserable, to chant constantly, since life may end any moment. Srila Prabhupada said studying his songs alone can make one Krishna conscious; Prabhu prays for surrender and dedication to the holy name. — “just once relish the nectar of the holy name.”

🎙 Prabhu at 39:12 (auto-transcript): “we see his mood of his dedication, surrender to the holy name in this bhajan that we sang earlier he is saying Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu sings in a very sweet voice Hare Krishna Hare Krishna Krishna Krishna Hare Hare Hare Rama Hare Rama Rama Rama Hare Hare And he is saying…”

Questions and comments at the end of the class.

🎙 Prabhu at 41:48 (auto-transcript): “Anyone has any questions or comments? Yes, he was also an administrator of the Jagannath Puri temple.”

children.topic: Q1 · Why outsiders can't enter Puri
children.note:
A devotee notes that Bhaktivinoda Thakur administered the Jagannath Puri temple and that Mahaprabhu went to Haridasa rather than demanding his entry, and asks the real reason outsiders are kept out.

🎙 Prabhu at 41:51 (auto-transcript): “Yes, he was also an administrator of the Jagannath Puri temple. Indians, they are not allowed to enter. He knew and he was a magistrate.”

In Mahaprabhu's time someone of Muslim birth would not enter a temple, so Haridasa stayed out. Later, after colonisers stole Subhadra's crown jewels and a temple prophecy spoke of foreigners taking Jagannath away, the temple barred anyone it does not authorise. Like Mahaprabhu, Bhaktivinoda Thakur simply followed the rules.

🎙 Prabhu at 43:08 (auto-transcript): “Well, during Mahaprabhu's time, obviously, if someone was from a Mohammedan background, they had no business going into a temple. That was the reason Haida Sarkur was not going in because he was known as being born in a Muslim family. But later on, closer to our times now,…”

If we are seeking justice in some personal matter, how do we pursue it while focusing on our relationship with Krishna?

🎙 Prabhu at 45:44 (auto-transcript): “So, Prabhu is saying we should seek Krishna. Our entire focus should be how to establish a relationship with Krishna And we may be seeking justice So how do we seek justice and connect with Krishna? Is that the question? So justice, if we have some personal issue where we are…”

As Sanjaya says at the Gita's end, victory and morality are wherever Krishna and Arjuna are. Bhaktivinoda Thakur trusted Krishna, suffered, and still won against the false Mahavishnu. Like the Pandavas, we seek guidance from scripture, prayer and authorities to know the right time. — “So justice is where Krishna is.”

🎙 Prabhu at 46:21 (auto-transcript): “So justice, if we have some personal issue where we are seeking justice And it's not connected to Krishna How do we go about it? In the Bhagat Gita, Sanjaya says, Yatra Yogeshwara Krishna, Yatra Partha Danurdhara, Tatra Shri Vijayor Bhutir, Dhruva Nitir, Mathir Mama. Wherever…”

maps.title: SB classes 2026 · Class 12 · When the Bee Sings

nodeData.note: SB 3.15.18 · a class by HG Sri Gauranga Das. In Vaikuntha even the great birds fall silent to hear a small bee glorify the Lord. Prabhu draws from this the spiritual world's variety and full consciousness, and above all its freedom from envy — the one fault that cannot be used in Krishna's service and that keeps us from tasting the Bhagavatam. The cure he gives is hearing and chanting in the association of sadhus, who help us see our faults and carry us home. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma describes how, when the king of bees sings the Lord's glories, the many birds of Vaikuntha pause their own sounds to listen. Vaikuntha is full of tumult — kolahala — because everyone is hearing and chanting, yet all fall quiet for the bee.

Brahma is describing what his sons the Kumaras saw on wandering into the Vaikuntha planets. Only one mood prevails there, service to Krishna; even the very attractive residents focus not on their beauty but on glorifying Him, and so do the non-human residents.

🎙 Prabhu at 03:52 (auto-transcript): “As the chapter is titled description of the kingdom of God we are hearing from Lord Brahma and how his sons the Kumaras were wandering all over the universe and eventually wandered into the Vaikuntha planets and so what they are seeing is what Lord Brahma is explaining here…”

Next to a peacock, or even a pigeon, the bee is tiny. But in Vaikuntha it does not matter who it is: if someone glorifies Krishna, everyone listens. — “whoever is glorifying Lord Krishna, we will hear.”

🎙 Prabhu at 11:17 (auto-transcript): “Now compared to a peacock, bee is small, isn't it? We see here there is a peacock mentioned. Or compared to even the other birds, smaller birds like the pigeons and the partridges, The bee is small. But Vaikuntha atmosphere is whoever is glorifying Lord Krishna, we will hear.…”

Many think the kingdom of God has no variety. Brahma's description shows many kinds of birds, bees and residents flying in vimanas that need no fuel.

🎙 Prabhu at 06:00 (auto-transcript): “And he's saying that there are many varieties. People usually tend to think that the kingdom of God, the spiritual world is without variety. There is one school of thought that teaches that there is no variety in the spiritual world. Many spiritual organizations or religions,…”

Some schools and near-death accounts describe only a tunnel and a light. But everything we see here and more is there, since this world is a perverted reflection of the spiritual one; those who say variety came from no variety have incomplete information. — “a perverted reflection of the spiritual world.”

🎙 Prabhu at 06:24 (auto-transcript): “Many spiritual organizations or religions, they tend to think that the spiritual world is just light, bright light. in contemporary literature also we find that people describe that they go through a tunnel and they see a bright light and then that's it it's just a bright…”

People call swans that carry passengers mythology. But Brahma was shown the spiritual world by the Lord and is an authority. Prabhu's example: someone from a developed country sees people queuing to pay electricity bills and says, back home we pay online; without hearing from such a person, we would say it cannot be.

🎙 Prabhu at 08:06 (auto-transcript): “but it is not mythology Lord Brahma not only has he seen himself the spiritual world he was granted the vision of the spiritual world when he shook hands with the supreme personality of Godhead he was able to see the whole spiritual world so he is an authority he has been…”

In his Brahma-samhita Brahma also describes the spiritual world: wish-fulfilling trees, no dust, everything made of precious jewels.

🎙 Prabhu at 09:30 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, Lord Brahma in his Brahma Samhita, he gives a description also of the spiritual world. Chintamani prakarasadma shukalpavriksha How there are wish-fulfilling trees there, how there is no dust, how everything is made up of precious jewels. And so here we see that…”

The first canto teaches that devotees accept words describing the Lord even when imperfect — with spelling or grammar mistakes, or unable to explain Him fully — because they are dealing with the unlimited Lord.

🎙 Prabhu at 11:52 (auto-transcript): “And therefore we find in the first cant of the Srimad Bhagatam, Suta Goswami mentions this point that words that describe the transcendental quality and nature of the Supreme Lord are accepted by those who are devotees. Even if these compositions that are done by devotees are…”

The birds raise their hearing and lower their own kirtana because they want to hear what the bee says about the Lord. Prabhu calls this the characteristic of a sadhu.

🎙 Prabhu at 13:09 (auto-transcript): “And that is what we are seeing here in the Vaikuntha atmosphere. The bee is singing, the other birds are hearing. They are keeping their shravanam to a high level and the kirtanam they have reduced. They want to hear what the bee is saying about the Lord. This is the…”

Here conscious means matter plus spirit, and unconscious means matter only, like stones. In the spiritual world there is no matter at all, so even what looks like matter is fully conscious.

🎙 Prabhu at 13:35 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, Srila Prabhupada is saying in the spiritual world, everything is conscious. There is nothing unconscious. In the material world, we have difference between conscious and unconscious. Conscious means that combination where there is matter plus spirit. And…”

Govardhan is a mountain but fully conscious, not like the Kilimambogo hills. Residents of Vaikuntha take whatever form pleases the Lord — even a bee, which here we think good only for honey — knowing themselves as His servants; their form is the form of service. — “Their consciousness is 100% Krishna conscious.”

🎙 Prabhu at 14:34 (auto-transcript): “We have an example just like Govardhan. Govardhan is a mountain. But because Govardhan is in the spiritual world, fully conscious. It's not stone like our Kilimambogo hills or something. Not conscious. No. In the spiritual world, everything is fully conscious because there is…”

We find it hard to grasp because we think in the duality of matter and spirit. In Vaikuntha there is no difference in purpose — everyone glorifies Krishna — so there is harmony, while here different agendas create disharmony.

🎙 Prabhu at 17:38 (auto-transcript): “because we are so conditioned and so used to thinking in terms of matter and spirit. This is the duality that we think in. But in Vaikuntha there is no duality. There are no two states. In the material world, everything is in duality because there is a difference between…”

children.topic: The Bhagavatam is for the non-envious
children.note:
The birds never ask who this bee is or why a bigger, more beautiful bird should listen. Likewise sadhus go to hear from whoever knows the science of Krishna.

🎙 Prabhu at 18:52 (auto-transcript): “as we have been discussing the sadhus they accept the glorification of Krishna therefore in the very first verse of the bhagatam Vyastev he writes he says this bhagatam is for the sadhus and who are the sadhus nirmat saranam satam the sadhus are those who have no envy nirmat…”
In the first verses of the Bhagavatam Vyasadeva says it is for sadhus free from envy, and invites relishers of rasa to drink its nectar. Only the non-envious can accept that invitation.

Bhaktivinoda Thakur, a district magistrate, did not expect people to come to him; he went to hear from Jagannatha Dasa Babaji. His designation did not matter when it came to hearing about Krishna.

🎙 Prabhu at 21:03 (auto-transcript): “Bhaktivinoda Thakur he was a district magistrate but he would go and hear from Jagannar Das Babaji Maharaj. Bhakti Vinod Thakur wasn't thinking I am a magistrate. People should come to me. People should hear me. No, he was going. The district magistrate designation was not…”

He sent his son Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur, a brilliant scholar who even wrote on astrology, to hear from Gaura Kishora Dasa Babaji, who could not write his name and signed with his thumb — 'angootha chhap' in Hindi and Gujarati.

🎙 Prabhu at 21:36 (auto-transcript): “And he instructed his own son Bhakti Siddhanta Sarasari Thakur go and hear about Krishna from go Kishrudas Babaji Maharaj. And who was Gorkeswar Das Babaji Maharaj? In modern contemporary estimation, he was illiterate. He didn't even know how to write his own name. He would…”

children.topic: Rama's bridge and the small helper
children.note:
As the vanaras hurled huge boulders into the ocean, a squirrel — some say a spider — carried tiny stones. Told to move aside before it got crushed, Lord Rama said both serve according to their strength and both are equal to Him. — “The service is what is important.”

🎙 Prabhu at 23:18 (auto-transcript): “We hear from Ramayan, when Lord Ram was to construct a bridge across the ocean to Lanka, where Ravan was holding Mother Sita. then the conclusion came that in order to build the bridge you will have to throw stones inside the ocean and then the ocean will hold the stones up…”

Commenting on this verse, Vishvanatha Cakravarti Thakur says envy is being unable to tolerate someone getting what I do not have — name, fame, position or recognition, tangible or not. 'Why did this devotee get that?' comes from envy.

🎙 Prabhu at 25:28 (auto-transcript): “What is the meaning of envy? Vishwanath Chakravitchi Thakur, when he is commenting on this verse, he says, envy means that I cannot tolerate the other person getting something that I don't have. Whether it is name, fame, prestige, position, power, recognition. If we are…”

The neighbour buys a fancy car while I cannot pay my electricity bill, so I want to go and scratch it. Nations, communities and individuals live this way because I want the recognition; that self-centred consciousness keeps us here, while Vaikuntha is centred on Narayana.

🎙 Prabhu at 26:39 (auto-transcript): “In the material world, we see it all the time. The neighbor got a new car and was able to buy that fancy car and I am struggling here day and night. I can't even afford to pay my electricity bill. Where did this guy get his money from? I'm going to go scratch his car now.…”

children.topic: The one fault Krishna can't use
children.note:
Devotees may think envy is only for others. Of lust, anger, greed, illusion, madness and envy, the acharyas say all can be engaged in Krishna's service except envy. It is why we are here, and why classes feel dry and nobody rushes to the Bhagavatam, unlike Bhakti's sons Jnana and Vairagya, who were rejuvenated by hearing it. — “Envy cannot be used.”

🎙 Prabhu at 28:05 (auto-transcript): “As practicing devotees, we may think, okay, yes, in the material world, everyone has envy. they are all envious of each other but we are devotees we don't have envy as practicing devotees we have to be very very careful because all the other inauspicious qualities in the…”

Krishna asks for constant remembrance, yet we finish our rounds and switch off. Envy is like cancer: everything looks normal while inside it grows, and by the time we detect it, it may be too late. — “But envy is like cancer.”

🎙 Prabhu at 32:14 (auto-transcript): “So we may think, oh yeah, okay, fine. I don't have envy. But envy is like cancer. Cancer, you may not know you have it until you know. By that time, sometimes it's even too late to do anything about it. Everything appears normal, inside everything is going wrong. You may not…”

Srila Prabhupada and the acharyas gave a process practised in the association of sadhus, who can see what we cannot see in our own hearts.

🎙 Prabhu at 33:13 (auto-transcript): “therefore Srila Prabhupada and our acharyas have given this process of Krishna consciousness wherein we practice in the association of sadhus sadhus can see we may not be able to see in our heart Or sometimes because of our pride, we may not even want to be willing to admit…”

If the doctor says you are sick and you call him a fake, how can you be helped — or if you diagnose yourself with ChatGPT and demand a prescription? Arjuna, elevated enough to name his weakness, said he did not know what was good for him and became Krishna's disciple. In devotee association subtle signs of envy surface, like thinking 'I can speak better'.

🎙 Prabhu at 33:44 (auto-transcript): “Like if you go to a doctor and the doctor says, oh, you know, you're sick, you need to do all these things. No, no, no, I'm not sick. You're a fake doctor. You just want to make money from me. I don't accept. Then how will you be helped? So if you want to be treated and you…”

Caitanya Mahaprabhu asked Ramananda Raya for the essence of the scriptures, and Ramananda humbly asked for His blessing to answer; Mahaprabhu also heard Svarupa Damodara sing. Srila Prabhupada would sit in class and ask his disciples to speak. — “That humility comes from non-enviousness.”

🎙 Prabhu at 35:57 (auto-transcript): “we see Chaitanya Mahaprabhu supreme personality of Godhead himself who did he go to hear from he went to Ramanand Rai and asked Ramanand Rai please tell me what is the essence of the scriptures and Ramanand Rai initially he was very perturbed he said you are supreme…”

A fisherman leaves his crab basket uncovered and tells a curious boy to look: whenever one crab climbs, another pulls it down. In an envious environment we become envious; Vaikuntha fosters appreciation and cooperation — the birds let the bee have its moment.

🎙 Prabhu at 39:15 (auto-transcript): “Now the question may come, but not everyone is so fortunate to have Sadhu Sangha or to have the right kind of association because association also matters, environment matters. If you are in an envious environment, you will end up envious. The example is given of crabs. There…”

Without good association there is still a solution, in the purport's last line: hearing and chanting. Hearing about devotees in the Bhagavatam, or chanting attentively, we can recognise our own faults and ask Krishna for help.

🎙 Prabhu at 41:20 (auto-transcript): “So, maybe we don't have that kind of environment. Maybe we don't have that fortune of associating with sadhus. What are we supposed to do then? Then, even there is a solution for that. And that's in the last line of the purport. The principles of devotional service, beginning…”

If we chant nicely, Krishna lights the lamp in the heart. In a dark room everything looks clean; switch on the light and you want to bolt. Seeing how much there is to deal with makes a devotee chant constantly and humbly, wishing others ahead rather than blocking them.

Fleeing the burning house of wax, giant Bhima carried his mother on his back and his brothers on his arms. Sadhus are like that: if you cannot go yourself they will carry you, provided you hear, chant and follow — as Srila Prabhupada said, hold on to my dhoti.

🎙 Prabhu at 44:44 (auto-transcript): “we were hearing from the Mahabharata Bhima was so big he was actually huge in today's day and age we'd call him a giant and what when it came time to run away from the house of wax as it was lit what did Bhima do? He was big, he was strong, he was fast. It was mentioned that…”

However turbulent the ocean, you are safe while on the boat; jump off and you are in trouble. There is a captain, crew and fellow passengers, and it is a joyful journey. — “as long as you are on the boat”

🎙 Prabhu at 46:08 (auto-transcript): “Then we don't have to do much. that is why ISKCON has been built it is like a boat however turbulent the ocean may be as long as you are on the boat you are okay you are safe the minute you start thinking no no this boat is going to drown let me jump then you are in trouble…”

Prabhu tells the ISKCON joke: newcomers call everyone Prabhuji, after initiation they are 'Das', then 'Prabhu', then 'Mahaprabhu'. Mahaprabhu's movement goes the other way — servant of the servant — and sadhus remind us of that. Where the bee is allowed to shine, love of Krishna does not just survive, it thrives.

🎙 Prabhu at 47:14 (auto-transcript): “we should never ever think that oh I know everything now I have read the Gita this many times I have read the Bhagatam this many times I have become you know there is that joke in ISKCON when someone joins first time they are always oh Prabhuji Prabhuji Prabhuji Prabhuji…”

Questions and comments at the end of the class.

🎙 Prabhu at 49:35 (auto-transcript): “If there are any questions or comments Yes Prabhu Everything in this material world is not conscious In the material world There is a difference between conscious and unconscious Material world means”

A devotee asks whether everything in this world is unconscious, and what of the holy places of pilgrimage.

🎙 Prabhu at 49:38 (auto-transcript): “Yes Prabhu Everything in this material world is not conscious In the material world There is a difference between conscious and unconscious Material world means Duality of matter and spirit”

Mayapur and Vrindavan are not part of the material world: step into the US embassy in Gigiri and you are in the US. But as in Srila Prabhupada's example of a bug on the king's throne, being there physically is not entering; if we see only hogs, noise and hotels, or tick sights off like a tourist, we have not entered Vrindavan. Narottama Dasa Thakur says go for sadhu-sanga. — “those are spiritual embassies that are here.”

🎙 Prabhu at 50:28 (auto-transcript): “Now you are asking about the Holy places of pilgrimage Within the material world They are not within the material world They are not on this earth. Mayapur, Vrindavan, those are spiritual embassies that are here. They are the spiritual world, not the material world. I think I…”

A devotee asks whether devotees themselves create envy through unequal treatment, such as some getting samosa while others get khichdi.

🎙 Prabhu at 54:04 (auto-transcript): “Yes. You said, don't you think we as devotees contribute a lot to become in this? For example, you only get samosa. Repeat the last part again. You think it's samosa or khichdi? If you are a devotee, whether it's samosa or khichdi, first thing you'll see is prasad. First…”

A devotee first sees prasadam. The bee does not complain it lacks peacock feathers. Fairness is the managers' job; individually we accept Krishna's mercy, and Krishna, who did not tolerate injustice to Ambarisha, will not tolerate it to us. Chase samosa and we leave Krishna; samosa is sold outside. — “Don't mind other people's business.”

🎙 Prabhu at 54:45 (auto-transcript): “Now, that's a very important point there. In devotional service, we mind our own business. Don't mind other people's business. You have been given khichdi, you eat your khichdi. Why are you looking at someone eating samosa? You don't need to see, oh, this person is eating…”

A devotee asks what to do when the very senior devotees one looks up to behave in ways that discourage.

🎙 Prabhu at 65:13 (auto-transcript): “Yes, Prahlad Prabhu. force are done by these same senior devotees.”

Devotees in the fourth canto pray only for pure association. Keep a respectful distance and work on yourself — Krishna has called that soul for some service. Like driving on a chaotic road, change roads or keep distance. Guru, sadhu and shastra are not bound by place: you are not a tree, you can move.

🎙 Prabhu at 66:12 (auto-transcript): “Yes, very good question. You are a crab in the basket, surrounded by other crabs. What do you do? You have to leave the basket. You have to find a conducive environment. And that is why we find that devotees all over in the Shastras, they are always praying to the Lord only…”

When a constant critic of Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur died, he asked who would now teach him humility. Sincere prayer brings the ability to see correctly or a better environment, so in devotional service we can never lose. — “It's all win-win.”

🎙 Prabhu at 70:46 (auto-transcript): “Bhakti Siddhanta Sarsiri Thakur and I end with this there was one person who was constantly arguing with him whenever he would speak this person is there he's blasting oh you said this criticizing arguing you know being very defiant and one fine morning that person wasn't…”

nodeData.topic: Class 13 · Desire, Karma and His Will
nodeData.note: SB 1.15.24 · a class by HG Sri Gauranga Das. Arjuna explains the Yadus' destruction as the Lord's will, and Prabhu widens it: behind nature's law of killing and protecting stands the Lord's supervision. Desires force us to work, our choice of pious or impious action brings reactions witnessed by the elements and the Supersoul, and the only way out is the third kind of action — work done for Krishna's pleasure, which frees us from karma and takes us home. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Arjuna tells Yudhishthira that everything happens by the Lord's will: sometimes living beings kill one another, sometimes they protect one another.

Arjuna had been away for months while Yudhishthira saw bad omens and feared a calamity. After recounting Krishna's many protections, Arjuna finally reveals that their relatives in Dvaraka are gone: cursed by a brahmana, they fought and killed one another while intoxicated.

🎙 Prabhu at 04:09 (auto-transcript): “Arjuna has finally told Yudhishthir Maharaj what has happened in Dwarka Arjuna was away from Hastinapur for over seven months and Yudhishthir Maharaj was worried during this time that why has Arjuna not returned and Yudhishthir Maharaj observed inauspicious omens in the…”

How could the Lord's family drink and kill each other? This mausala-lila has many reasons, but Arjuna sums it up: the Lord wanted His family to leave this way. — “This is due to the will of the Lord.”

🎙 Prabhu at 05:43 (auto-transcript): “So sometimes this particular pastime of the Lord known as Mushalalila may not be easily understood. How is it that the Lord's family were drinking? And how is it that they fought and they killed each other? How do we understand this? Therefore, Arjuna in today's verse is…”

Living beings do this all the time; Srila Prabhupada calls it the struggle for existence and survival of the fittest. But the world is not working on its own. — “No, there is the Lord's supervision behind it.”

🎙 Prabhu at 07:00 (auto-transcript): “But in reality, living entities do this all the time. Therefore, Arjuna is saying here that sometimes they protect one another and sometimes they kill one another. This is the law of this world. And Prabhupada is saying, survival of the fittest. But even behind this law of…”
Krishna says in the Gita that material nature works under His supervision, producing moving and non-moving beings.
Peace or war comes about because we must act: under the modes of nature no one can sit idle even for a moment. — “We are forced to work.”

Ask a child if he wants to go to school to study, a young adult if he wants to go to work, a middle-aged man if he still wants to — the natural answer is no, or 'I wish for a holiday'. Our nature is not to work; desires force us.

🎙 Prabhu at 09:11 (auto-transcript): “So then the question comes, why should we work? If you ask a child, do you want to go to school, to study? they may want to go to school but not to study to play but if you ask a child do you want to go to school to study the first natural response is no you ask a young adult…”

The Lord has no desires and needs nothing; if He does desire, it is fulfilled at once. Our original nature as His parts is also to be satisfied, but we have forgotten it and now try to fulfil our desires here.

🎙 Prabhu at 10:31 (auto-transcript): “if the lord has desires our vedic scriptures they tell us first of all the lord has no desires He is completely self-satisfied. He doesn't need anything, doesn't want anything. That is the first point. He is self-satisfied. He is okay. He doesn't want or need anything. But if…”

To eat one rasgulla you need milk — good luck in Kenya's milk shortage — so a cow, grass, land and workers, plus sugarcane, sugar processing, fire and something to curdle the milk. You even need another living being to give the milk. We are not independent, though most people say 'I am in control'; the Lord alone has no constraints.

🎙 Prabhu at 12:00 (auto-transcript): “we are trying to fulfill our desires so i always give this example you want to read or eat you want to eat a rashagula you have a desire i want to eat rashagula which is a sweet can you fulfill that desire on your own can you just sit and say i want to eat rashagula and then…”

To fulfil desires we act, and action is only of two kinds, pious and impious. But who decides which is which?

🎙 Prabhu at 15:07 (auto-transcript): “And activity is of two types. There are only two types of activities we can do. Pious and impious. The question comes, okay, who is to decide what is pious and what is impious? If I see my neighbor has grown some grass and he is not going to eat it because he doesn't have a…”

If I take my neighbour's unused grass to feed my cow, I call it pious; he calls it theft. Scriptures differ on which animals may be eaten, and some countries drive on the right while others drive on the left — so who says what the law is?

🎙 Prabhu at 15:19 (auto-transcript): “The question comes, okay, who is to decide what is pious and what is impious? If I see my neighbor has grown some grass and he is not going to eat it because he doesn't have a cow, I can just go take the grass and give my cow. That's a pious activity because I am feeding the…”

Ajamila, pious early on, spent most of his life robbing and cheating to maintain his family. On his deathbed three grotesque figures came to drag him out of his body, and he screamed for his son Narayana; the Lord at once sent His messengers. — “but luckily his child's name was Narayan.”

🎙 Prabhu at 16:34 (auto-transcript): “in the Srimad Bhagatam we hear of a person who was pious in the beginning of his life but towards the end of his life majority portion of his life he spent performing impious activities he was looting people on the road performing all sorts of cheating violence to maintain…”

Asked on what basis they take a person, the Yamadutas answer that scripture defines piety and impiety, and scripture comes from the Supreme Lord Himself. So the choice of pious or impious means is ours, and each has its repercussions.

🎙 Prabhu at 18:14 (auto-transcript): “And so in that conversation, the messengers of the Lord, they asked these messengers of the God of death, these grotesque looking people who are the messengers of God of death. And they asked him, how do you come and take a person? What basis do you have to come and take a…”

children.topic: Bread from God or the party
children.note:
Srila Prabhupada told how in communist countries, in wartime hunger, people leaving church after praying for daily bread were met by party members with crates of loaves: your God gave you nothing, we give you bread. One can pray for bread or steal it; the choice decides the reaction.

🎙 Prabhu at 19:54 (auto-transcript): “Krishna Prabhupada was mentioning that in the communist countries people would go to church and they would say the lord's prayer our father who art in heaven hallowed be thy name thy kingdom come it will be done on this earth as it's done in heaven give us today our daily…”

Once we act, a result must come, and when it comes we cannot complain — though it may not come immediately.

🎙 Prabhu at 21:22 (auto-transcript): “So according to the desire, we perform activity. That activity is classified either pious or impious. And once we perform the activity, then there has to be a result. And when we get that result, then we cannot complain. However, the result may not be immediate. Sometimes…”

Slap someone and he may not slap back, but wait for the day the one slap becomes ten. Years later you ask why — remember ten years ago?

🎙 Prabhu at 21:56 (auto-transcript): “Sometimes when you go and slap one person, usually you get a slap back. But someone may not slap back. They say, I will wait for that day. When this one slap will turn into ten slaps to you. And so, out of the blue, you get such a day coming. and then you ask, why you did…”

You may be good in this life, but what about the previous one? The Lord supervises that every action gets its reaction; that is the law of karma. — “The law of karma is every action has a reaction.”

🎙 Prabhu at 22:34 (auto-transcript): “So therefore the popular question comes, why do bad things happen to good people? But you are good in this lifetime. What about the previous lifetime? What did you do then? How did you choose to perform your activities? And therefore, the Supreme Lord, he supervises and he…”

Someone plants a mango seed, forgets it, and finds a fruiting tree decades later. As they say, to eat mangoes your grandfather should have planted the tree. The Lord fixes each action's gestation period — sometimes lifetimes.

🎙 Prabhu at 23:18 (auto-transcript): “And because of time, this may not be immediately apparent. Just like someone goes and puts a mango seed in the ground and forgets about it, comes after 50 years and he finds a beautiful mango tree with ripe mangoes on it and says, oh, how did this happen? Or the son comes and…”

Like sneaking a rasgulla from the deity kitchen and asking who saw you, we may ask who witnessed past-life deeds. The Yamadutas answer: the elements, each with a person behind it, like the sun god, the same sun since creation. Wherever you hide there is space, wind and earth. — “all these elements they witness our activities”

🎙 Prabhu at 25:16 (auto-transcript): “so therefore the question comes then okay I may have done some impious bad activities but who was the witness who saw why am I getting a reaction if I cannot even put up a defense as to whether I did that activity or not so this question was also asked to the messengers of…”

The Lord in the heart is the overseer and the one who gives permission. He does not interfere with our choice, but once it is made we cannot change the reaction — like boarding a plane to Mombasa and wanting to get off halfway because you meant to take a matatu. — “You can't get down midway.”

🎙 Prabhu at 27:05 (auto-transcript): “apart from that there is the Lord in the heart Lord Sri Krishna tells us I am situated in the heart and he says this many times in the Gita I am situated in the heart and I am witnessing everything in the body the supreme lord is situated as as super soul and what does he do…”

children.topic: The third option: work for Him
children.note:
Besides pious and impious action, the Gita teaches a third: action for the Lord's pleasure, which brings no good or bad reaction. Prabhu names the three karma, vikarma and akarma, and the Lord advocates akarma.

🎙 Prabhu at 29:22 (auto-transcript): “but there is a third option apart from these two activities pious and impious there is the third option which the Lord teaches in the Gita the third option is performing activity for the pleasure of the Lord yajyarthat karma non yatra loko yam karma bandana tadartham karma…”
Krishna says work done for Vishnu's satisfaction does not bind.

How do we know what pleases Him? He tells us Himself: whatever we do, eat, sacrifice or endure, offer it to Him. Then actions are free of reaction, the Lord is pleased, and we leave the sphere of forced work.

In His abode there are no factories and no office hours; everyone pleases the Lord and enjoys, and wish-fulfilling trees answer any desire. But the one desire there is to please Him.

🎙 Prabhu at 32:01 (auto-transcript): “The Lord tells us If you surrender on to me You can come out from this world Where we have to perform activity And go to a world where there is No need to perform any activity There is only one Work or activity there And that is enjoy You don't hear In the kingdom of God…”

Why a price? It is the Lord's home: as a guest in a Vedic home leaves his shoes outside, the entry condition is to serve and live with Him. For any other desire He mercifully gave us this world to try our best. — “Because that's the Lord's home.”

🎙 Prabhu at 34:21 (auto-transcript): “entry. Now someone may say, but why is the Lord doing that? Why does he have this rule? Why should it be like this? No, he should let everyone come. Why is there a price for entry? Because that's the Lord's home. Just like when someone comes to a home, usually in Vedic…”

Our desires clash with others', so we protect those aligned with us and fight those against us — what Arjuna describes. Krishna says the only change needed is from 'I want to enjoy' to 'let me help the Lord enjoy'; then action and reaction stop, for the spiritual world has devotion, not karma. — “the only thing we need to change”

🎙 Prabhu at 35:35 (auto-transcript): “so we are here we have desires these desires are conflicting with other people's desires and so therefore we end up either killing one another or protecting one another if my desire is lining up with your desire we will protect each other if my desire is fighting with your…”

This is karma-bhumi, the land of action. Refuse to work and you still must eat; refuse to eat and you leave this body for another — perhaps one that cannot even think about these things — and are forced to work by its programming. So it is in our interest to learn what pleases the Lord.

🎙 Prabhu at 36:58 (auto-transcript): “Here in the material world is known as karma bhoomi. You may have come across this term somewhere. Karma bhoomi. The place of performing activity. And so because we are forced to Lord Krishna tells us someone may say no I don't want to be forced. I'm not going to work he says…”
The Lord loves us and never forces; we are stubborn. Krishna says the souls struggling here are His own parts, and He pleads with us to come home, where there is no work and no reactions.

Told not to open the cupboard, a child insists, hurts his fingers and runs crying to his mother, who does not say 'sort yourself out'. We insisted on enjoying apart from the Lord and got kicked around, yet He comes Himself, sends His devotees and the Bhagavatam and Gita to call us back. — “You've got kicked enough, come back”

🎙 Prabhu at 39:21 (auto-transcript): “like a small child you know, he wants to open a cupboard and the mother tells him hey you will hurt your fingers like no, you will hurt your fingers don't open the cupboard, no ok go open the cupboard and then he opens the cupboard, he hurts his fingers gets pain, starts…”

Coming here, and getting out, are both the Lord's will, because without Him we cannot do anything. If we link with Him and act for His pleasure we leave the cycle of action and reaction — the art of doing a thing perfectly.

🎙 Prabhu at 41:12 (auto-transcript): “and therefore Arjuna is saying here Ishwarasya vicheshtitam all this is the will of the Lord we come here also the will of the Lord we get out also the will of the Lord because without him we can't do anything we can't even eat one rasgula simple thing he gives us the teeth…”

children.topic: He gives the teeth and hands
children.note:
We cannot even eat one rasgulla on our own: He gives the teeth, the hand to pick it up and the intelligence to make it. Yet, puffed up by false ego, we think 'I am doing'.

🎙 Prabhu at 41:32 (auto-transcript): “we can't even eat one rasgula simple thing he gives us the teeth to eat he gives us the hand to pick up the rasgula he gives us the intelligence to make a rasgula he gives us everything yet we think prakriti kriyamanani gunai karmani sarvasa I am doing We become puffed up…”

An industrialist shows his empire as the fruit of his hard work. The intelligent person sees that many others helped, and without Krishna's mercy nothing would have happened.

🎙 Prabhu at 42:14 (auto-transcript): “Sometimes we go to some industrialists and say, you see all this I did I worked hard, it's my hard work that you are seeing today, I did this But the devotee understands the intelligent person understands oh not only you did so many other people helped you not only that…”

Questions at the end of the class.

🎙 Prabhu at 43:47 (auto-transcript): “any questions or comments yes Matthew”
Matthew asks, as far as can be heard, about other religions' ways of dealing with reactions, such as forgiveness of sins, and whether they have means to please the Lord.

children.topic: Every bona fide religion pleases God
children.note:
Religion has three parts — the Lord, His devotee and devotional service — so a bona fide religion always has practices to please Him, like the Ten Commandments. A rose smells as sweet by any name; Srila Prabhupada said he came not to convert but to teach how to love God. — “It's not for our pleasure.”

🎙 Prabhu at 46:00 (auto-transcript): “The first point being that if we are saying it's a religion, religion has three aspects. there is the supreme lord there is his devotee and then there is devotional service Bhagawan Bhakta Bhakti so if someone is saying that I am following a particular religion then that…”

We do not do Tulasi parikrama to cut karma, planning a sin today and parikrama tomorrow; Parikshit compares that to an elephant bathing and then throwing mud on itself. Freedom from karma is a side effect; the motive is the Lord's pleasure. — “it is about pleasure of the Lord”

🎙 Prabhu at 50:13 (auto-transcript): “so we are not saying oh if only you do tulsi parikrama your karma will be cut we are not doing tulsi parikrama for karma to be cut because if karma is cut there then tomorrow you will go and do other karma you will get other reaction this is what Parikshit Maharaj and this is…”
